properties.description:
SVRGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northern Hart County in northeastern Georgia...
West central Anderson County in Upstate South Carolina...
Southeastern Oconee County in Upstate South Carolina...

* Until 415 PM EDT.

* At 310 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Seneca,
moving south at 15 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind
damage to trees and power lines.

* Locations impacted include...
Reed Creek, Lake Hartwell, Fair Play, Townville, Oakway, and
Sadlers Creek State Park.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

If on or near Lake Hartwell, get away from the water and move
indoors or inside a vehicle. Remember, lightning can strike out to
15 miles from the parent thunderstorm. If you can hear thunder, you
are close enough to be struck by lightning. Move to safe shelter
now!  Do not be caught on the water in a thunderstorm.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

Please report damaging winds, hail, or flooding to the National
Weather Service by calling toll free, 1, 800, 2 6 7, 8 1 0 1, or by
posting on our Facebook page, or post it to X using hashtag nwsgsp.
Your message should describe the event and the specific location
where it occurred.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Mountains
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued June 1 at 12:58PM MDT until June 2 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of central New Mexico, including the following
area, South Central Mountains.

* WHEN...From late Tuesday morning through early Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rich Gulf moisture will surge over the area Tuesday producing
numerous showers and thunderstorms. A few of the stronger storms
will be capable of producing rain at rates over 1 inch per hour.
Locations below recent burn scars will be especially susceptible
to rapid runoff and flash flooding.
- The south central mountains, including Ruidoso.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued May 31 at 11:49AM AKDT until June 3 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Kodiak Island. This includes the
cities of Kodiak City, Port Lions, Ouzinkie, Old Harbor.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff from heavy rain may result in flooding
of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone
locations, including Bells Flats. Expected heavy rain may saturate
soils resulting in isolated landslides in areas of steep terrain.
Strong east to northeast winds gusting to near 60 mph at times may
also result in downed trees due to saturated soils.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An unseasonably strong North Pacific low south of Kodiak
Island is expected to bring an atmospheric river of moisture
across Kodiak Island Monday morning through Tuesday night. 2
to 4 inches of rain is possible along the eastern coast of
the island with 3 to 6 inches of rain possible for the higher
terrain. 1 inch or less of rain is possible across the
western coast of the island. The heaviest rain is expected to
fall between noon Monday and noon Tuesday, with the bulk of
the expected storm total rainfall falling during this time.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

- All residents on or near mountain slopes should be prepared for
possible landslides.
